hypothesis: Holding the S&P 500 members with the strongest 12-month gains (skipping the latest month), equal-weighted and rebalanced monthly, beats both SPY and an equal-weighted S&P 500 after costs.
rationale: Medium-term momentum (Jegadeesh and Titman 1993) is among the most replicated return patterns. Skipping the latest month avoids short-term reversal. Comparing with the equal-weighted universe separates the momentum effect from simply equal-weighting smaller S&P members. Prior evidence on this data: 126-day momentum showed a weak positive raw IC (t about 1.6), so a strong result is not expected.

signal.description: return from 252 to 21 trading days ago

prior_evidence: 126-day momentum had a weak positive raw IC; this 12-1 construction was not tested.
decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 24 months against SPY. If any gate fails: close H4; do not try other lookbacks, skip periods or portfolio sizes on this data.
